eips.title: Builder Execution Requests
eips.summary: Cited in chat as solving the builder-validator deposit coupling issue after the Glamsterdam fork.

moments.context: Nico Flaig noted in chat that EIP-8282 solves the builder onboarding deposit problem after the fork, implying the current issue is temporary.

eips.title: Disallow new 0x00 validators
eips.summary: Barnabas proposed changing EIP-8365 so mistaken 0x00 deposits are not burned but instead create inactive validators.

moments.context: Barnabas introduced his concern that the current EIP burns ETH for post-fork 0x00 deposits, including those already in the pending queue from before the fork, and proposed allowing those validators to join without duties instead.

NC agreed that deposits submitted before Hegota should be grandfathered and suggested moving the guard from apply_pending_deposits to process_deposit_request; discussion was deferred for further review.

eips.title: Optional Execution Proofs
eips.summary: Discussed at length whether to CFI optional execution proofs for Hegota; ultimately left as DFI despite support from some teams.

moments.context: Ignacio presented slides on EIP-8025 readiness across EL and CL clients, arguing for CFI to upstream the execution specs PR and reduce branch maintenance burden.
Lightclient argued in chat against spending time on non-critical non-PQ topics, suggesting optional proofs be shipped without a core EIP.
Lightclient spoke against CFI, saying all large Ethereum features had to wait on their own branches for years; Ignacio countered that CFI would streamline spec integration.
Potuz strongly opposed forcing clients to implement an optional feature and objected to merging it into the Heze fork branch, as it would constrain all future EIP writers.
Stokes concluded there was not enough CL team consensus to CFI; the EIP was marked DFI for today, with a note to explore better spec processes.

eips.title: RowDAS - Distributed Blob Reconstruction
eips.summary: Csaba presented RowDAS, referred to by name only and never by number; DFI'd for Hegota on low client support.

moments.context: stokes opened the item as "RowDAS" with no EIP number given at any point on the call.
Csaba described the goal as fixing two PeerDAS design decisions: excess CPU load on large nodes and the protocol's reliance on those nodes.
Csaba offered a reduced "B option" that fixes only the CPU load, via in-protocol duty allocation.
stokes read the client rankings: Nimbus in favor; Teku, Lighthouse and Grandine against; no ranking from Lodestar or Prysm.
With no client team speaking in support, stokes DFI'd it for Hegota, noting blob supply and demand make it not the most urgent EIP.

eips.title: Custom sweep threshold for validators
eips.summary: Dima noted in chat that EIP-8148 and EIP-8205 needed discussion but no substantive discussion occurred on the call.

moments.context: Dima said in chat that EIPs 8148 and 8205 needed to be discussed, opposing a suggestion to default-DFI all remaining EIPs.

eips.title: Beacon Block Reporting Field
eips.summary: Beacon block reporting field for client diversity data was presented by Luca; DFI'd due to lack of strong client support.

moments.context: Luca from Vero described the proposal to add a dedicated beacon block field for client diversity reporting, arguing graffiti is inadequate for complex multi-node setups.
No CL teams spoke in favor; stokes DFI'd the EIP, noting the topic is important but support is insufficient for Hegota.

eips.title: Anti-Correlation Attestation Penalties
eips.summary: Oisin Kyne presented anti-correlation attestation penalties and asked for CFI; insufficient CL team support led to DFI.

moments.context: Oisin Kyne presented EIP-7716, explaining the proposal to increase inactivity penalties when many validators are offline simultaneously, to incentivize client diversity.
Łukasz Rozmej expressed concern that nobody would notice the penalty cap until a big outage; Oisin argued the financial impact would change behavior.
Stokes concluded there was not enough strong CL team support to CFI; the EIP was DFI'd for Hegota.

eips.title: Withdrawal credentials preregistration
eips.summary: Dima presented withdrawal credentials preregistration to fix delegated staking front-running; decision deferred to next call.

moments.context: Dima Gusakov presented EIP-8205, explaining the front-running vulnerability in delegated staking deposits and proposing a preregistration system contract similar to EIP-7002 and EIP-7251.

Matthew Keil from Lodestar argued the problem is already solved at the app layer and suggested waiting for PQ deposit contract changes; Dima countered that the issue affects the majority of staked ETH across many protocols.
Greg from Lido requested the final decision be deferred to the next call since time was insufficient; stokes agreed to revisit at the start of next call.

eips.title: Execution layer triggerable withdrawals
eips.summary: Referenced as precedent for the system contract pattern proposed in EIP-8205.

moments.context: Dima cited EIP-7002 and EIP-7251 as existing system contracts similar to what EIP-8205 would introduce for preregistration requests.

eips.title: Increase the MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE
eips.summary: Referenced alongside EIP-7002 as precedent for the system contract approach in EIP-8205.

moments.context: Dima cited EIP-7251 and EIP-7002 as existing system contracts that the preregistration request contract would closely follow.

eips.title: Beacon block root in the EVM
eips.summary: Referenced as the mechanism through which EIP-8205 preregistrations can be proven on-chain.

moments.context: Dima explained that depositors can prove via EIP-4788 that a preregistration exists, guaranteeing correct withdrawal credentials upon deposit.
